Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //vwvw.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 55 s. 2023 AUG 30 HON. SANTIAGO B. CANE, JR. Governor Province of Agusan del Sur Dear Gov. Cane, Jr.: This has reference to your letter requesting for a legal opinion on whether officials and/or employees may validly act on routine and non-routine office transactions by affixing their digital signature while on personal leave, on official business, or on off days. With the enactment of Republic Act No. 9792 or the Electronic Commerce Act of 2000 provided legal recognition of electronic signatures and consequently imposed strict requirements before an electronic signature qualifies as a handwritten signaturel. Moreover, Executive Order No. 810, series of 2009, institutionalized the Certification Scheme For Digital Signatures and Directing the Application of Digital Signatures in E-Government Services. The Civil Service Commission (CSC) in its MC No.24 s. 20172 on the 2017 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions, particularly on Sec. 13 par (c) on Designation provided the following: Designation - movement that involves an imposition of additional and/or higher duties to be performed by a public official/employee which is temporary and can be terminated anytime at the pleasure of the appointing officer/authority. Designation may involve the performance of the duties of another position on a concurrent capacity or on a full-time basis. A designation in an acting capacity entails not only the exercise of the ministerial functions attached to the position but also the exercise of discretion since the person designated is deemed to be the incumbent of the position. Officials designated as Officer-in-Charge (OIC) enjoy limited powers which are confined to functions of administration and ensuring that the office continues its usual activities. The OIC may not be deemed to possess the power to appoint employees as the same involves the exercise of discretion which is beyond the power of an OIC, unless the designation order issued by the proper appointing officer/authority expressly includes the power to issue appointment. 1 sec. 8 of RA 8792 2 24 August 2017 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.•. 8876-34-54

Designation shall be governed by the following rules: xxx xxx xxx (3) For positions with incumbents who temporarily can not perform the duties of the position (vacation or sick leave, study leave, scholarship, maternity leave, special assignments), the designations should be synchronized with the absence of the incumbent, unless earlier revoked or recalled by the appointing officer/authority. However, the designation of employees may be renewed every year in the exigency of the service but not to exceed (2) years. (4) For positions without incumbents, a designation may be made only for a maximum of one (1) year. However, the designation of employees may be renewed every year in the exigency of the service but not to exceed two (2) years. (5) Designations shall be made through an Office Order issued by the appointing officer/authority concerned. (6) For designation to critical positions in the local government units such as Provincial/City/MunicipaI Government Department Head, a copy of the office order shall be furnished by HRMO of the LGUs to the CSCFO concerned. Employees designated to positions with duties involving practice of profession shall be required to possess the necessary professional license. Further, the CSC in its Omnibus Rule on Leave3 provided that an official or employee on vacation or sick leave (personal leave), a substitute appointment or an OIC can be temporarily designated in his position. Sec. 64. Status of the position of an official or employee on vacation or sick leave.- While the incumbent is on vacation or sick leave or without pay, his position is not vacant. During the period of such leave therefore, only substitute appointments can be made to such positions. It bears to note also that this Department through its Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2019-21 re: Operational Guidelines and Rules in Implementing Administrative Order No. 15 Series of 20184 provided the policies and procedures in the implementation of AO 15 in temporary vacancies, multiple or otherwise in local elective offices. The MC supplemented RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 in order to ensure uninterrupted delivery of basic services to the local constituents. Pertinently, it provides that when a temporary vacancy exists in the office of the governor, the vice governor, or in case of his/her inability, the highest-ranking sangguniang panlalawigan member, shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the governor, except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Based on the foregoing, we are of the view that a public official or employee cannot perform the duties of his office during his/her leave of absence. Such leave of absence is understood to be the type of leaves enumerated in Civil Service Form No. 6, Revised 2020. 3 Rule XVI of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of EO 292 4 February 12, 2019. Page 2 of 3

The same is true with regard to affixing their signatures while on off days. Considering that a public official/employee cannot perform their functions while on personal leave more so during days which are not considered as working days, the consequent affixing of their signature on the aforementioned days would produce no effect and hence, improper. Verily, this Department is of the view that a public official or employee can validly act on routine and non-routine office transactions by affixing their digital signature while on official business, which requires the public official/employee's attendance. In addition, sufficient documentation to support the official business is necessary in order to validly act on such documents. This opinion is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATT .J ICTOR R.
